_comment_purpose: Lane C, C-03: put Cosys-AirSim into PX4 EXTERNAL-AUTOPILOT mode so PX4 SITL flies the
vehicle over the MAVLink Simulator API, while PX4's own uxrce_dds_client exposes the
SAME /fmu/* topics Lane A produces. MAVLink drives the sim physics handshake; XRCE-DDS
drives the autonomy code. Coupling: lane-c-topic-parity.
Passed with --settings rather than dropped in ~/Documents/AirSim/, so the config is a
reviewable repo artifact instead of per-machine state.

UE frame trips PX4 SITL timeouts - the documented fragility of this integration.

_comment: PressureFactorSigma tweak from upstream's PX4 docs: reduces barometer drift so
GPS lock and EKF2 convergence happen quickly instead of stalling the run.

_comment_params_deliberately_absent: Upstream's PX4 example sets NAV_RCL_ACT=0 and NAV_DLL_ACT=0 to disable the RC-loss
and datalink-loss failsafes. NOT done here, deliberately.
Lane A leaves the GCS-datalink check ENFORCED (NAV_DLL_ACT=2, set by the x500
airframe) and satisfies it with a real QGroundControl service, because PX4 refusing
to arm without a datalink is a property of the real aircraft too. Disabling it in
Lane C would make the two lanes diverge exactly where sim-to-real parity matters,
and would hide an arming failure that the real Pixhawk 6C would still have.
Consequence: arming in Lane C will need a datalink the same way Lane A does. That is
the intended behaviour, not an oversight.
